work.title: Das Lied von der Erde
work.movement: III. Von der Jugend — Behaglich heiter

version.note: The item does not say which score edition the orchestra used or whether any passage was cut. The first edition (Universal Edition, 1912) is the score read for the notes on this page; the 1939 performing materials may differ.

performers.note: The item credits Kerstin Thorborg (alto), Carl Martin Öhmann (tenor) and Carl Schuricht (conductor) for the whole concert, and names the singer on each track; Kerstin Thorborg does not sing in this song. The Mahler Foundation’s discography lists the same three with the Royal Concertgebouw Orchestra, Amsterdam. The orchestra was not yet styled “Royal” in 1939.

date.note: The date is in the item’s title and date field and agrees with the Carl Schuricht article; the Mahler Foundation gives only “October 1939 broadcast concert, live”. It is not the upload date (the item was added on 2 July 2022).

place.note: Named in the item title (“Concertgebouw Amsterdam”) and in the Mahler Foundation’s listing of a live Amsterdam concert; “Concertgebouw” names both the orchestra and the hall, and neither source names a room.

label.note: The item names no label and does not state the medium it was copied from. The Mahler Foundation’s discography records a Bel Age CD made “from acetates” of the broadcast; whether this file derives from that issue is not stated.

catalogue.note: No catalogue number is given for the source of this file.

matrixTakeSides.note: No acetate matrix, side or take numbers appear in the sources consulted; this is not a claim that they cannot be recovered.

credits.note: The item names an uploader account but no transfer or restoration engineer; an uploader is not automatically a transfer engineer.

date.note: The item’s added and public dates (2 July 2022) are upload dates, not transfer dates.

processing.value: Internet Archive derivatives of a WAV original: this file is a variable-bit-rate MP3 (178 kbps); FLAC and spectrogram derivatives of the same WAV are also listed.
processing.note: The item description calls it “a good recording”. It does not describe noise reduction, speed correction or equalisation.

digital.format: VBR MP3 (178 kbps) derivative supplied by the Internet Archive; original upload WAV

composition.value: Music by Gustav Mahler (died 1911); words adapted by Mahler from Hans Bethge’s Die chinesische Flöte (Bethge died 1946). The 1912 first edition is published public-domain material on IMSLP.
composition.note: A term calculation (life plus 70 years; Bethge’s text has been free in life-plus-70 jurisdictions since 2017), not a clearance of every edition or translation.

recording.value: Treated as public domain in the European Union (territorial): a live broadcast of 5 October 1939 whose related rights expired well before the extended term applied on 1 November 2013. United States status is not established.
recording.note: Under Directive 2006/116/EC as amended by Directive 2011/77/EU, a performer’s right for a performance of 1939 ran 50 years from the performance (to 1989), or, if a phonogram fixation was lawfully published or communicated to the public in that time, 70 years from that event (to 2009); the 70-year terms apply only to rights still alive on 1 November 2013 (Article 10(5)). The CD issues came later. The item carries a Public Domain Mark 1.0 licence URL, which is the uploader’s statement and not the basis used here.
